meta.heading: Round 7: polishing the alpha against modern apps
meta.intro: I went through every screen of the alpha and compared it with how apps like Toggl, Todoist, Linear and Sunsama handle the same job. The look and motion hold up well; these cards are the small frictions worth fixing next. The full review is in [Shiftbook UI/UX review](https://claude.ai/artifact/G6HhC9X4WjonRat2hQjoTL). The sign-up screen bug (text too big, the code check needing a scroll) is being fixed separately.

r7-enter.title: Enter logs it, and typing a time works in the Log work box
body: Today, pressing **Enter** in the Log work box only shows "Pick a time button". Every modern tracker commits on Enter, and Shiftbook's own capture box already understands "50m" or "1.5h". The paste-then-15m/30m/1h flow you approved stays exactly as it is; this only adds a faster path.
bullets: Type `INC0045678 50m` and press **Enter**: logged as 50 minutes.
Paste a ticket with no time and press **Enter**: focus jumps to the time buttons, and the arrow keys pick one.
A **Same as yesterday** row under the box shows yesterday's routine entries (daily meeting, general tickets) as one-click buttons.

questions.legend: Enter in the Log work box

options.value: Logs it, or jumps to the time buttons

r7-enter.pick: Both. Every step saved is one less reason to skip logging.

r7-find.title: Find things again from the capture box
body: The capture button says **Log, note or find**, but finding isn't built yet. Linear, Raycast and Notion all open one box that searches everything and runs commands. In Shiftbook it would be the same capture box:
bullets: Type a ticket number or a word: matching entries, days and Inbox scraps appear under the line. Enter opens the one you pick.
Type a command such as **Lock**, **Book holiday** or **Timesheet** to do it straight away.
Logging still works the same: a line with hours in it logs, as today.
r7-find.pick: Search and commands. "Which day was that ticket?" is the question a work log should answer fastest.

r7-views.title: Number keys and the greyed-out views
body: The view switcher shows five tabs, but Planner and Canvas are greyed out until they're built. Keys **1, 2, 3** open Desk, Timesheet and Customize, so pressing **2** opens the fourth tab. The ribbon layout from round 5 doesn't change either way.

questions.legend: Until Planner and Canvas are built

options.value: Hide them, and 1 to 3 match the tabs
Keep them greyed out, renumber the keys to 1, 4, 5
Move it behind a gear button and Ctrl+,
options.why: How most apps do settings; leaves the tabs for your work.

r7-views.pick: Hide the unfinished views so what you see is what works, and keep Customize where it is for now.

r7-target.title: Your own daily target, a text size option, easier-to-read grey
bullets: **Daily target:** the ring on the Desk always measures against 8 hours. A setting per weekday (for example 4 h on Fridays) lets a short day still close the ring.
**Text size:** Small, Normal or Large next to Theme and Motion. Some labels are 10 to 11 px today.
**Contrast:** the light grey used for hints and "No project" is a little too faint to read comfortably. A slightly darker grey fixes it; colours otherwise stay the same.
**Undo:** the Undo toast stays for 10 seconds instead of about 5, and waits while the pointer is over it.
r7-target.pick: All four. They're small and they make the app kinder on long days.

r7-wrapup.title: A gentle end-of-day wrap-up, and marks for days with nothing logged
body: Two ideas borrowed from Sunsama and Toggl. Neither nags: both can be turned off in Customize.
bullets: **Wrap-up card** at a time you choose: hours logged today, anything without a timesheet code, the tray total, and one line for "tomorrow I start with…".
**Gap marks:** weekdays on the ribbon with nothing logged get a small dot. Clicking one opens capture for that day.
r7-wrapup.pick: Both, with the wrap-up off until you switch it on.

r7-firstrun.title: Setup, unlock and the recovery key in the same paper look
body: The first screens you see (create password, recovery key, unlock) still use the plain style from before the look was decided, with bigger text and thicker borders. That's why sign-up feels oversized. Bringing them onto the same paper cards as the app makes the first impression match, and the recovery key would sit in a compact grid with **Copy** and **Save as file** beside it, like 1Password's recovery kit.

options.value: Just fix the size bug for now

r7-firstrun.pick: Yes, after the sign-up bug fix lands, so the two changes don't collide.

r7-polish.title: Small fixes I'd fold in along the way
bullets: A **shortcut sheet** on the **?** key listing every key.
The **+15m / +30m / +1h** buttons on an entry also show when it's selected with the keyboard, not only on hover.
A **This week** button on the Timesheet to jump back after browsing.
Tab stays inside capture and the details panel while they're open.
Plainer names where internal words leak through, for example "Inbox zero".
r7-polish.pick: Yes. None of them changes anything you've already approved.
